title: Interactive Cost & Fidelity Sandbox — PRD and Launch Playbook
author: Leah Moreno
body:
Overview
--------
This document defines the Product Requirements and launch playbook for the Interactive Cost & Fidelity Sandbox (ICFS), a developer-facing environment that lets engineering and product teams run realistic, query-level simulations of Redwood inference consumption to evaluate cost, latency, and quality tradeoffs before committing to a deployment or capacity plan. ICFS unifies: a lightweight local runtime, a cloud-backed simulation harness, fidelity profiles, and telemetry-driven cost modeling into a single interactive UX and programmatic API.

Motivation
----------
Teams building LLM features need fast, reproducible answers to questions like: 
- What is the per-10k-token cost for conversational workloads at our expected distribution of prompt lengths and response lengths?
- How does quantization (Q4, Q8) affect output quality on our prompt set?
- Which batching and KV cache configuration meets our 200ms P50 latency target while minimizing cost?

Existing tools produce static estimates or require heavy manual traffic replay. ICFS provides a repeatable, interactive way for developers, SREs, and solutions engineers to run scenario experiments against the same fidelity and telemetry models Redwood uses in production.

Goals (what success looks like)
--------------------------------
1. Developers can generate an end-to-end consumption estimate (cost, latency, model-variant mix, and quality delta) for a supplied prompt set within 2 minutes.
2. The scenario simulation matches production billing signals within +/- 7% for token-based routes and within +/- 10% for embedding-heavy workloads for standard fidelity profiles.
3. Provide a web-based interactive UX and a programmatic API (OpenAPI) that supports: sampling, deterministic traffic replay, and sensitivity analysis for batching, KV cache hit rates, and quantization.
4. Integration with Redwood Console telemetry so simulations can be saved, shared, and used to suggest Dedicated sizing recommendations (initial alpha).

Non-goals
---------
- ICFS will not be used as a production traffic proxy or gateway. It is strictly for simulation and estimation.
- The first public release will not support every third-party model adapter; we will ship with the top 6 model families used by Redwood customers.

Stakeholders and ownership
---------------------------
- Product lead: Leah Moreno (owner)
- Eng lead: Ravi Kapur (eng-serving-runtime)
- UX/Design: Dana Li (eng-developer-experience)
- Applied ML / Evaluations: Omar Ruiz
- SRE & Capacity: Priya Sinha
- Sales & Solutions enablement: Marcus Holt

User personas
-------------
- Individual engineer: quick back-of-envelope estimates for feature design.
- ML platform engineer: sizing Dedicated pools and choosing quantization policies.
- Solutions engineer: create shareable scenarios for customer onboarding and purchase conversations.

High-level feature set (MVP)
----------------------------
1. Interactive UI: scenario builder with source prompt upload (CSV/JSONL), selection of model variants, fidelity profiles, and target SLA (latency P50/P95).
2. Programmatic API: simulate endpoint that accepts a prompt set, configuration JSON, and returns: per-token cost estimate, latency distribution, token breakdown (input/output), and a quality delta score for user-supplied evals.
3. Local runtime shim: Docker image + lightweight CLI that can (optionally) replay traffic locally using a small model or the Redwood lightweight kernel for offline experiments.
4. Fidelity profiles: presets (high, standard, cost-optimized, quantized-q4) with exact parameter definitions (attention kernels, KV caching assumptions, float vs quantized memory footprint).
5. Telemetry mapping: simulation outputs include the same telemetry labels used in Console (route, model_variant, tenant_id) to allow upload & comparison.
6. Shareable scenario artifacts: human-readable summary, JSON export, permalink into Console for stakeholders with appropriate RBAC.

Functional requirements (detailed)
----------------------------------
FR-1: Scenario ingestion
- Accept CSV/JSONL with fields: id, prompt, expected_response_length_hint (optional), metadata (optional).
- Validate schema and sample distribution (report basic statistics: token length histogram, top n prompt types).

FR-2: Simulator core
- Simulate per-request tokenization, prefix KV hit (configurable hit rate), batching policy, and model kernel selection.
- Use production-derived latency models per model_variant and GPU class.
- Produce per-request traces including: tokens_in, tokens_out, kernel_path, simulated_latency_ms, and cost_usd.

FR-3: Quality delta evaluation
- Accept an eval harness (small labeled set) and compute a quality delta for each fidelity profile using BLEU/ROUGE or a user-specified metric.
- Return aggregated quality delta and per-example diffs (truncated) for manual review.

FR-4: API and UX results
- Provide results via interactive UI and a JSON API. API responses must include summary and a per-percentile latency and cost table.
- API must be authenticated via Redwood API keys and honor tenant scoping when used in cloud mode.

FR-5: Export and Console sync
- Allow scenario export as a JSON artifact and optional upload to Console workspace. Linking should preserve scenario metadata and attach telemetry tags.

Non-functional requirements
----------------------------
NFR-1: Accuracy targets
- Cost estimates within +/-7% of production for token routes across standard fidelity profiles.
- Latency percentiles within +/-12% for P50/P95 when using the same model_variant and hardware class.

NFR-2: Performance and scale
- Cloud simulation cluster must support 200 concurrent scenarios (each up to 10k prompts) without queueing beyond 3 minutes.

NFR-3: Security and privacy
- Uploaded prompts are treated as customer data, stored encrypted at rest when stored more than 24 hours.
- Provide an option to auto-delete artifacts after scenario completion.

API contract (example)
---------------------
Request (POST /v1/simulate):
{
  "tenant_id": "tenant_abc123",
  "model_variant": "redwood-v2-small-quant-q4",
  "fidelity_profile": "cost-optimized-q4",
  "prompts_url": "s3://.../promptset.jsonl",
  "config": {
    "kv_cache_hit_rate": 0.65,
    "batching_policy": "latency-optimized",
    "target_latency_ms": 200
  }
}

Response (200):
{
  "summary": {
    "estimated_cost_usd": 12.43,
    "p50_latency_ms": 182,
    "p95_latency_ms": 521,
    "mean_tokens_per_response": 64
  },
  "breakdown": [ /* per-request rows truncated in API response; full artifact available as downloadable archive */ ]
}

Telemetry and observability mapping
----------------------------------
The simulator emits the following telemetry fields to match Console: route, model_variant, scenario_id, fidelity_profile, kernel_path, sim_latency_ms, sim_cost_usd, tokens_in, tokens_out.

Telemetry table (example):
| field | type | description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| route | string | customer-defined route name |
| model_variant | string | model variant used in simulation |
| scenario_id | string | ICFS scenario GUID |
| fidelity_profile | string | preset name |
| sim_latency_ms | number | simulated end-to-end latency |
| sim_cost_usd | number | simulated cost per request |

Quality scoring notes
---------------------
- The baseline release will support BLEU and ROUGE and a Redwood internal embedding-similarity delta for semantic drift.
- Scoring must be configurable to allow customers to supply their own scorer function in the harness (lambda or local script in the local runtime mode).

UX flows and wireframe notes
---------------------------
1. Onboarding: quick wizard to upload prompts, pick target fidelity profile, select model variants, and pick summary metrics to produce.
2. Run: progress bar with early preview: after 10% of prompts simulated the UI shows a provisional estimate.
3. Compare: side-by-side fidelity profile comparison with toggles for batching and KV cache assumptions.
4. Share: generate permalink with access control and option to attach to a Console project.

Pricing & packaging guidance (alpha recommendations)
--------------------------------------------------
- Beta access will be free for self-serve tenants up to 5 scenarios/month.
- For scale usage we will meter scenarios as a blend: compute-time (per-sim-minute) + storage for saved artifacts. Example rate: $0.10 / sim-minute + $0.02 / GB-month for artifacts beyond 30 days.
- Enterprise customers with Dedicated contracts: include 1,000 sim-minutes/month as part of the SLA bundle and custom pricing for on-prem sandbox appliances.

Launch & rollout plan (90 days)
------------------------------
Phase 1 (30 days): internal alpha
- Deliver core simulator, local runtime, and internal UI.
- Run 20 internal scenario validations against production telemetry and adjust latency/cost models.
- Success gate: accuracy within targets on 3 sample tenants.

Phase 2 (30 days): closed beta
- Invite select customers and Solutions engineers.
- Add Console integration for scenario save/share.
- Collect feature requests and telemetry comparison artifacts.

Phase 3 (30 days): public beta
- Self-serve onboarding, documentation, and SDKs.
- Release pricing and create playbook for Sales.

Release notes template (for each public release)
------------------------------------------------
- New fidelity profiles added (list)
- Accuracy model updates and calibration notes
- API changes (contract, new fields)
- Known limitations and recommended workarounds

Operational runbooks & support
------------------------------
- Runbook: ICFS service health page, SLOs, common alerts (simulation-queue-depth > 30, model-latency-drift > 20% vs baseline).
- Support playbook: how to convert a scenario into a Dedicated sizing recommendation and handoff to SRE for capacity reservation.

Open risks and mitigations
-------------------------
1. Drift between simulator models and production kernel behavior (risk): mitigate with continuous calibration job that re-benchmarks kernels monthly.
2. PII in prompt uploads (risk): mitigate via auto-redaction option and strict retention defaults.
3. Overreliance by customers (risk): label estimates as guidance and include confidence interval and calibration scores on all outputs.

Next steps / immediate action items (owner: Leah)
------------------------------------------------
1. Finalize fidelity profile definitions with Applied ML (due: 2026-03-01).
2. Build initial latency/cost model skeleton and validate against two production tenants (due: 2026-04-01).
3. UX wireframes and CLI UX (due: 2026-04-08).
4. Prepare closed beta customer list and Solutions enablement kit (due: 2026-04-15).

Appendix: example scenario summary
--------------------------------
Scenario: "Customer X conversational helpdesk"
- Prompts: 5,432 JSONL objects, median prompt tokens = 28, median expected response tokens = 46.
- Selected model variants: redwood-v3-small, redwood-v3-medium-quant-q4
- Results (simulated): estimated monthly cost (100k queries/day): $8,420; p50 latency = 198ms; quality delta vs baseline = -1.4% (semantic similarity).
